chinchilla_paper.title: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models (Hoffmann, Borgeaud, Mensch, Buchatskaya, Cai, Rutherford, de Las Casas, Hendricks, Welbl, Clark, Hennigan, Noland, Millican, van den Driessche, Damoc, Guy, Osindero, Simonyan, Elsen, Rae, Vinyals, Sifre; 2022)
chinchilla_paper.revision: arXiv:2203.15556v1 (only version listed on the abstract page, submitted 29 Mar 2022)
chinchilla_paper.text: atlas/papers/chinchilla/paper.txt (our extraction of https://arxiv.org/html/2203.15556 via html_to_text.py; the fetched HTML is kept as _arxiv_2203.15556.html; no PDF downloaded)
chinchilla_paper.anchor_convention: chinchilla:§3.2 (section), chinchilla:§abstract, chinchilla:eqN (equation number as in the HTML: 1-4 main text, 5-11 Appendix D.2), chinchilla:tableN / chinchilla:tableA3, chinchilla:figN / chinchilla:figA1. No page anchors: the HTML carries no page breaks.
chinchilla_paper.note: Every anchor quote is a verbatim substring of paper.txt; inline math appears there as $...$ so quotes avoid or include it exactly. `python3 discover_paper.py --check` verifies all quotes (atlas/tools/check_anchors.py skips non-line refs). discovered.json lists the numbers that disagree inside the paper (MMLU 67.5 vs 67.6; Table 3 rows vs §3.4 prose for 175B/280B; Gopher FLOPs 5.76e23 vs 6.3e23).
